atoms.b: Glass is ((++hard soft)) and has a very smooth surface. In addition, it is usually ((++transparent opaque)), which makes it an ideal material for windows and food containers. However, glass can also ((++shatter smile)) easily.

In its solid state, glass does not warp, is resistant to most ((++chemicals rocks)), and can be cleaned easily. That’s why containers and tools made from glass are often used in ((++chemistry PE)) experiments.

Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: People have been making glass for 4,000 years. Glass is made by heating sand or rocks that contain quartz to a very high temperature. The individual grains melt together and leave a hard solid when they cool.
The precise ingredients vary depending on the intended use of the glass. At a very high temperature of around 1,700 degrees Celsius, the sand melts and becomes a glowing, viscous mass.

instruction.text: Match the pictures to the techniques for shaping molten glass.

feedback.end: Flat objects made from glass, for example window panes, are usually finished using rollers.
Simple objects without decoration, such as glasses and bowls, are made by putting the molten glass into a mould.
Glass-blowers can make very colourful, ornate objects by blowing air into partially molten glass through a tube.

instruction.text: Put the journey of a glass bottle in order. Start at the top with “a bottle is cast in a mould”.

atoms.text: A bottle is cast in a mould.
The bottle is filled with a drink.
The bottle is delivered to a shop and a customer buys it.
The empty bottle is dropped off at the bottle bank.
The glass waste is transported to a recycling facility.
The glass waste is sieved and melted down to be used again.
